correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in \(y\) and \(z\) give \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid y]=1-by\) and \(\mathbb E[x\mid z]=-cz\). The first law implies the support ceiling \(y\le1/b\). Stationarity of \(z^2/2\) and \((x^2+z^2)/2\) gives \(\mathbb E[\dot z^2]=c\mathbb E[x^2(a+1/c-y)]=bc\mathbb E[(1/b-y)(a+1/c-y)]\). Zero defect makes \(z\) and \(x\) constant on support trajectories and bounded completeness reduces the remaining coordinate to the known equilibrium set. The weighted-mean bounds and undershoot consequence then follow exactly. The packaged checker verifies the critical polynomial algebra.

value.rationale: The model's literature emphasizes parameter-dependent chaos, recurrent attractors, and the economic roles of interest rate, investment demand, and price index. The accepted theorem supplies exact stationary constraints valid independently of which compact recurrent component is sampled: investment demand has a sharp stationary support ceiling, mean-square price-adjustment speed equals a signed product of distances from the two natural equilibrium demand levels, and zero adjustment is rigidly equivalent to equilibrium support. In the three-equilibrium regime every genuinely time-dependent stationary state must undershoot the nonzero-equilibrium investment level, while the interest-rate-squared weighted demand is confined to a parameter-explicit interval. These give structural consistency tests and a global recurrent-geometry consequence rather than a local bifurcation or numerical re-estimation.
